A fraud rule flags a refund as "issued before the payment it refunds." The audit log agrees: payment at 10:00, refund at 08:05 the same day. In reality the refund came five minutes after the payment. The payment API runs on a VM set to UTC+2, the refund worker runs in a container on UTC, and both stamp events with
. Each value is a correct reading of a different clock, and the log column keeps only the reading.

It's a half-truth. On one machine, in one time zone, with no clock change in between,
values do order events correctly. Most apps start exactly there, so the bug shows up later: a second region, a container, a cloud host on UTC, or the night the clocks change.

Local time is not a timeline
Local clock time can repeat and skip. In zones with
, one night a year the clock goes back an hour, so the same local reading happens twice; on another night an hour of local time never exists.
arithmetic doesn't check whether a local value is ambiguous or invalid, and it ignores the zone's adjustment rules. An admin changing a server's time zone has the same effect. So
values aren't guaranteed to be in order even on a single machine.
